title: PU-12M lesson 4: the operator-plotter
status: A seat lesson (docs/TUTORIALS.md): step by step, each control highlighted, the next step only once it is done.
source: sam3d; the moves are the console's procedures (data/procedures/pu12m.json: deploy_map) and the plotting by hand (simcore/command_post.hpp PlotAt, data/gameplay/plotting.json); the plotter's spoken reports (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 23); docs/research/PLOTTING_BOARD_2026-10.md; the plotter on FuG-1 himself, his headset on PVS-1, and the radiotelephonist's journal (docs/research/PLOTTING_BOARD_2026-10.md, 'How the plotter got the picture'; pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 24)
notes: The post starts deployed; the targets come in on cue.

steps.title: The operator-plotter's seat
lines: You are the operator-plotter (No. 2): on the bench, in the middle.

The radar company reads the air picture out on the air-picture net, target by target, out to 200 km. You hear it in your headset, plugged into the radiotelephonist's box (PVS-1) beside you, on the same set as he is. He writes every report in the journal open on his table; when you miss one, it is on that page. You write each target on the plotting board, so that the battery commander sees what is coming long before it is near, and you call each new target to him aloud: he sits beside you.
Each step lights up what to use; only that works. Read, then Enter.

steps.title: The plotting board
lines: Before you: the plotting board, a sheet of plexiglass etched with range circles every 50 km and the grid's squares, the post at its centre. It is folded on its hinge for the march.
steps.hint: L: look at it.   Enter: next.

steps.title: Open the board
lines: Click the latch on the board's frame: you swing the board open before you on its hinge.
steps.why: Folded, nothing can be written on it.

steps.title: The IT-45 tube
lines: At your right: the IT-45, the battery commander's tube, with the regiment's telecode picture out to 100 km. It is his: you write what you hear, and the board is his picture beyond the tube, and when it is dark.
steps.hint: L: look at it.   Enter: next.

steps.title: Listen
lines: A target comes in. Listen: the radar company reads its report on the net, in your headset and in amber on the screen: its number, its square of the grid, its type and size, its height and the minute.
The line fades after a few seconds: remember the number and the square. Missed it? Look at the radiotelephonist's journal: it is written there with the time he heard it.

steps.title: Pick it: the mouse wheel
lines: Look at the board and turn the mouse wheel: the numbers of the reports you have heard come up one at a time beside your cross. Stop at the one you just heard.
steps.why: A report you don't write within a minute is gone: the next one is coming.
steps.hint: Mouse wheel over the board: the next number.

steps.title: Plot it: click its square
steps.wait_text: the target written on the board
lines: Click on the board where the report put it: its square. The first two digits are the big square (labelled on the grid), then the ninth of it (1 2 3 along the top, 8 9 4 across the middle, 7 6 5 along the bottom), then the ninth of that.
Within 5 cm of the right place your mark goes exactly there; further off, it lands off the target, and the commander reads it where you put it.
steps.why: The commander warns the launchers and gives them targets from the board.

steps.title: Call it to the commander: «Новая цель …»
steps.wait_text: the target written on the board
lines: The commander decides on what you tell him. Say each new target aloud as you write it: its number, bearing and range from the post, height, identity and size. O, then the report line, filled in from your board.
steps.why: Uncalled, he finds it only on his next look over the board, half a minute on; called, he has it at once (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 17, 23).
steps.hint: O: your reports, then the highlighted line's number.

steps.title: Another
lines: A second target comes in: listen for its report.

steps.title: Pick it and plot it
lines: Wheel to its number, click its square. Each target is reported again about once a minute: write each new report, and its crosses make its track.
steps.hint: Mouse wheel: the number.   Click: the mark.

steps.title: Call the second one
lines: And the second: O, then «Новая цель …». A target that turns you report the same way («Цель … развернулась»), and one the net stops reporting («Цель … потеряна»).
steps.hint: O: your reports, then the highlighted line's number.

steps.title: Keep plotting: the commander gives a target
lines: Keep the board up to date: every report as it comes, each new target called, a turn or a lost target reported.
The battery commander reads your board: each track's range and when it will be here. He gives a target to a launcher on the battery net once it is within reach: listen.
steps.why: He gives targets only from marks under two minutes old: an old mark is where the target was, not where it is.

steps.title: The operator-plotter's part: done
lines: That is your part: the air picture's reports, heard in your headset (or read off the radiotelephonist's journal), written on the board target by target, and each new one called to the commander.
Esc, then M: the missions menu, and the next seat's lesson.
